instrument_name: Texas Constitution Art. VIII s.24-a (individual income tax prohibited) and s.24-b (capital gains tax prohibited)
authority: Texas Legislative Council (tcss.legis.texas.gov official statutes file server)
figure_or_rule_carried: 24-a: the legislature may not impose a tax on the net incomes of individuals (added Nov. 5, 2019). 24-b: no tax on realized or unrealized capital gains of an individual (added Nov. 4, 2025). No state wage income tax, no state withholding, no state W-4, no state W-2 filing.

instrument_name: Texas Labor Code ch. 62 Texas Minimum Wage Act (minimum wage, tipped employees, local preemption, exemptions)
figure_or_rule_carried: 62.051: employer pays the federal minimum wage under FLSA s.6 (no separate state rate; USD 7.25 via FLSA). 62.0515: state minimum wage supersedes local ordinances on private-employment wages (except public contracts). 62.052: tipped employee wage = FLSA 3(m) cash wage; tipped = more than USD 20/month in tips. 62.151: chapter does not apply to a person covered by the FLSA. Exemptions 62.152-62.160 (religious, professionals, domestic, under-18 non-graduates, students under 20, inmates, family members, seasonal amusement, non-UI-liable employers except agriculture, dairy and livestock).

instrument_name: Texas Labor Code s.62.003 Earnings statement (Texas Minimum Wage Act)
figure_or_rule_carried: At the end of each pay period the employer gives each employee a written earnings statement, signed by the employer or agent, showing: employee name; rate of pay; total pay earned in the period; each deduction and its purpose; net pay; total hours worked (hourly) or units produced (piece rate). Any form; may be on the check voucher. Scope: ch. 62 does not apply to persons covered by the FLSA (62.151), so the duty binds only for employees outside FLSA coverage. Corrects the 'no pay-statement statute' line of US-TXR3-001 / US-TX-LAB-001 (those read ch. 61 only).

instrument_name: Texas Labor Code ch. 61 Payment of Wages (Texas Payday Law) - local copy
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages include vacation, holiday, sick, parental leave and severance pay owed under a written agreement or written policy (61.001(7)(B)). FLSA-exempt employees paid at least monthly, others at least twice a month, equal periods (61.011); default paydays 1st and 15th, paydays posted (61.012). Final pay: discharge by the 6th day after discharge; resignation by next regular payday (61.014). Commissions/bonuses per agreement (61.015). Payment in cash, negotiable instrument, EFT to employee-designated account or payroll card (61.016); direct deposit needs 60-day written notice (61.017(c)); payroll card: 60-day notice, fee list (English or the card's language), opt-out form, alternate payment by first payday after 30 days (61.017(d)-(e)). Deductions only by court order, law, or written authorization for a lawful purpose (61.018). Same instrument as US-TXR3-001, now with a local file.

instrument_name: Texas Labor Code s.1.005 Preemption (H.B. 2127, 88th Leg. 2023)
figure_or_rule_carried: A municipality or county may not adopt, enforce or maintain an ordinance regulating a field occupied by the Labor Code, including employment leave, hiring practices, breaks, employment benefits, scheduling and other terms of employment that exceed or conflict with federal or state law (for private employers). No state paid sick leave statute exists; local paid sick leave ordinances are void under this section.

instrument_name: Texas Labor Code ch. 51 Employment of Children
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum age 14 (51.011). Ages 14-15: max 8 h/day and 48 h/week; no work 10 p.m.-5 a.m. before a school day, midnight-5 a.m. otherwise and in summer recess (51.013). Certificate of age available from TWC (51.022). No minor-specific pay rule beyond the 62.155 minimum-wage exemption.

instrument_name: Texas Unemployment Compensation Act ch. 201 (employer, employment, wages)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer: USD 1,500 wages in a quarter or 1 worker in 20 weeks (201.021); state and political subdivisions are employers (201.026); domestic: USD 1,000 cash wages in a quarter, optional annual reporting due Jan 31 (201.027); farm and ranch labor per 201.028/201.047. Excluded: church/religious-order service and ministers (201.066), student service at own school and co-op programs (201.069), H-2A workers unless FUTA covers them (201.078). Wages include non-cash remuneration and FUTA-taxable tips (201.081); exclude above USD 9,000 per employee per calendar year (201.082(1)) and employer retirement/sickness/medical plan payments, 401(a)/403(a) payments, employer-paid FICA (201.082(2)-(6)).

instrument_name: Texas Unemployment Compensation Act ch. 204 Contributions
figure_or_rule_carried: No employee UI deduction (204.003). New employer rate = greater of major-group rate less 0.1 pt or 2.6% (204.006). Replenishment rate reduced by 0.1 pt from 2006 (204.0625) to offset the Employment and Training Investment Assessment of 0.1% of wages, collected with contributions (204.121). Enhanced wage filings: wage, industry, occupation, full/part-time, county of primary employment, remote-work status (204.0025, amended by S.B. 1786, H.B. 120 and H.B. 2, 2025).

instrument_name: Texas Constitution Art. XVI s.28 Garnishment of wages
figure_or_rule_carried: No current wages for personal service are subject to garnishment except to enforce court-ordered child support or spousal maintenance (federal levies, federal student loans and other federal debts apply by federal law).

instrument_name: Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code s.63.004 Current wages exempt
figure_or_rule_carried: Except as otherwise provided by state or federal law, current wages are not subject to garnishment; garnishee discharged as to current wages.

instrument_name: Texas Family Code ch. 158 Withholding from earnings for child support
figure_or_rule_carried: Max 50% of disposable earnings (158.009). Start no later than first pay period after delivery (158.202). Remit each pay date to the State Disbursement Unit; employers with 50+ employees by EFT/EDI within 2 business days after pay date, up to USD 25 surcharge per non-electronic remittance (158.203). Employer admin fee up to USD 10 per month from disposable earnings (158.204). Multiple orders: equal shares of current support first, then arrears (158.207). Termination notice within 7 days (158.211). Withholding also from severance and lump-sum payments (158.214-158.215).

instrument_name: Texas Family Code ch. 234 subch. B State directory of new hires
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers report each newly hired or rehired employee to the state directory operated by the Title IV-D agency (Office of the Attorney General) with TWC, per 42 U.S.C. 653a (234.102); procedures by OAG rule (234.104); civil penalty up to USD 25 per unreported employee, USD 500 if conspiracy (234.105). Deadline not in the statute (see OAG page row).

instrument_name: Texas Business and Commerce Code s.501.001 Certain uses of social security number prohibited
figure_or_rule_carried: Private persons may not make an SSN available to the public, print it on access cards, require its transmission over a non-secure Internet connection, or print it on material sent by mail unless law requires it (501.001(a)); exceptions for uses required by law and internal verification or administrative purposes (501.001(e)). No pay-statement-specific SSN truncation rule.

instrument_name: Texas Election Code s.276.004 Unlawfully prohibiting employee from voting
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer may not refuse time off to vote on election day or during early voting, nor penalize it; 'penalty' includes loss or reduction of wages, so the time off is paid. Exception: polls open two consecutive hours outside the employee's working hours.

instrument_name: Texas Government Code ch. 2258 Prevailing Wage Rates - local copy
figure_or_rule_carried: Same content as US-TXR3-002 (public body sets the prevailing per diem rate; USD 60 per worker per day penalty; contractor records of name, occupation, per diem wages); this row adds the local file.

instrument_name: Texas Employer New Hire Reporting Form and instructions (OAG Child Support Division, REV 05/23, 1 TAC 55.303)
authority: Office of the Attorney General of Texas - Child Support Division
figure_or_rule_carried: Report within 20 calendar days of the employee's first day of work. Required boxes: 1 FEIN (same as on quarterly wage reports), 3 employer name (as on W-4), 4 employer address for income withholding orders, 5-7 city/state/ZIP, 14 SSN, 15 date of hire (first day services performed for wages; rehire = return date), 16-18 first/middle/last name, 19-22 employee address. Optional: TWC account number, phone, fax, contact, state of hire, DOB, salary and salary frequency. Channels: online employer.oag.texas.gov, fax, mail (Central File Maintenance, PO Box 12048, Austin 78711-2048), telephone. Penalty USD 25 per unreported employee, USD 500 conspiracy.

instrument_name: TWC Texas Guidebook for Employers - New Hire Reporting Laws
authority: Texas Workforce Commission (Office of the Commissioner Representing Employers)
figure_or_rule_carried: New and rehired employees reported within 20 calendar days of hire; electronic reporters may instead report at least twice a month, 12 to 16 days apart. Minimum content: company name, address, FEIN; employee name, SSN, address; first day of paid work. Second document family to US-TXS5-016 for the 20-day rule.

instrument_name: TWC Texas Guidebook for Employers - Accrued Leave Payouts
authority: Texas Workforce Commission (Office of the Commissioner Representing Employers)
figure_or_rule_carried: Accrued leave payout at separation is owed under the Payday Law only if a written policy or agreement promises it, and on its terms (Labor Code 61.001(7)(B)). An acquisition is a separation that triggers a written payout policy. Lump-sum payments of USD 500 or more (bonus, payment in lieu of leave) by an employer holding an administrative writ in a IV-D case require prior notice to the OAG and a 10-day hold or OAG authorization (Family Code 158.215; OAG online lump-sum notification form).

instrument_name: TWC unemployment tax estimator page (efte) - local copy 2026-11-02
figure_or_rule_carried: Same content as US-TX-P5-2-002, now with a local file: employers in their first six calendar quarters generally pay the new-employer rate 2.70%; deficit tax 0.00% for 2026; obligation assessment 0.01% for 2026; rate applies to the first USD 9,000 of each employee's earnings; official rate notices mailed by the Tax Department each year (2027 not yet published on 2026-11-02).
